title: Pay-per-use vs Pro pricing explainer — job-card pile-up, live price comparison, feature grid, the math, checkout, end card

source.author: @thayto_dev
source.note: Remade from scratch in HyperFrames after the AjustaCV Pro video; structure and pacing follow it. Brand, prices, features and numbers are fictional placeholders in US dollars — replace every one with your real plan before publishing.

scenes: serif hook rises line by line while ten job cards fly in and stack up with a live counter
pay-per-job receipt fills row by row and its total counts up; the Pro card's price per job drops with every row; a green banner says when Pro has paid for itself
the total is struck through; the Pro card turns into the blue 'What you get with Pro' tile
five feature cards with small UI illustrations appear one by one and get a check
dark slide: what a week without the job costs, counted up, against what Pro costs per day
checkout card builds line by line; its button grows until it fills the screen
blue end card: mark, wordmark with plan badge, two-line tagline, URL pill
notes: Money is formatted from cur + dec (use cur 'R$ ' and dec ',' for Brazilian reais). The receipt total is perJob x rows and the Pro line is monthly / rows, so keep perJob, monthly, the banner, the savings pill and the checkout copy consistent with each other: the defaults are $2.90 per job, $29 for 6 months ($4.83 a month), $7.29 month to month (34% more). The small UI inside the feature cards is drawn in the ILL array; its labels are English and not variables. Long lines shrink to fit their space.
